messages:
lucy: Heads up, trying to set up redwoodctl on a fresh Pop!_OS VM. Ran the install script but `redwoodctl` is not runnable: `permission denied` when executing /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl.

omar: Did you `curl | sh` or use the pkg? paste `stat -c '%a %n' /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl`

lucy: output: `644 /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` so it's not executable. Installer didn't set +x for me.

omar: Strange. Some installers respect umask or the extracted file mode. Workaround: `sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl`. Also check if /usr/local is mounted with noexec. `mount | grep /usr/local`.

lucy: chmod fixed it, binary runs now. But `redwoodctl profiles list` returns empty and `redwoodctl login` complains "no profiles configured" even though I previously used the cloud UI and expected an auto-created default.

kate: Which config/version? We used to write to `~/.config/redwood/profiles.json` and then switched to `~/.redwood/config.json`. Newer CLIs should migrate automatically but the installer sometimes skips migration if it runs in an odd order. Run `redwoodctl doctor` to see detected schema.

lucy: doctor says: "legacy config detected at ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json (schema v1)" and suggests `redwoodctl migrate-config --source ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json`. I ran it, profiles now appear.

ben: FYI there's a headless-friendly login flow: `redwoodctl login --no-browser` will print a code and a URL you can open elsewhere. Also `--device` does the same.

lucy: used `--no-browser`, completed auth on my phone. But `redwoodctl local-serve --profile default` still failed with `no token found` because my token was at `~/.config/redwood/token.json`. Moved it to `~/.redwood/token.json` and local-serve recognized it.

omar: We'll add a resiliency patch to detect legacy token/profile paths at runtime so rare installer skips don't break local dev.

devbot: branch created: `fix/cli-config-legacy-detection`. CI pipeline triggered, unit tests added for migration and `--install-dir` behavior. :hammer_and_wrench:

kate: Also adding docs note about `--install-dir` for users whose /usr/local is noexec, and a test that verifies the installer sets executable bits regardless of umask.

lucy: One more edge-case I hit: if you `sudo mv` the binary from a temp dir, ownership can be root and permissions preserved; recommend using the install script or `--install-dir $HOME/.local/bin` for non-root installs.

ben: Thanks, all. Good coverage. Closing once CI green. :thumbsup:
